headline: 18 goals: Messi becomes World Cup's all-time top scorer after brace vs Austria
summary: The 38-year-old captain led Argentina to a 2-0 victory, securing a spot in the knockout stage while breaking the global scoring record.
details: Lionel Messi has become the most prolific scorer in World Cup history, netting 18 goals across his career. The milestone was reached during Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria on Monday.

Despite missing an early penalty, Messi scored twice to secure the victory. His first goal in the 38th minute leveled him with Brazilian legend Marta, while a second goal in stoppage time set the new global benchmark.
The Argentine captain's performance also matched a rare milestone, making him one of only three players to score in six consecutive World Cup matches, alongside Just Fontaine and Jairzinho.
Currently leading the 2026 World Cup Golden Boot race with five goals in the tournament, Messi described the record-breaking night as 'spectacular' despite feeling 'very tired' after the match.
With six points from two matches, Argentina has now safely advanced to the last 32 of the tournament with a game to spare.
caption:
18 goals and a new world record! 🐐

Lionel Messi has officially become the most prolific scorer in World Cup history.

Lionel Messi has become the most prolific scorer in World Cup history, netting 18 goals across his career. The milestone was reached during Argentina's 2-0 win over Austria on Monday.

Despite missing an early penalty, Messi scored twice to secure the victory. His first goal in the 38th minute leveled him with Brazilian legend Marta, while a second goal in stoppage time set the new global benchmark.

The Argentine captain's performance also matched a rare milestone, making him one of only three players to score in six consecutive World Cup matches, alongside Just Fontaine and Jairzinho.

Currently leading the 2026 World Cup Golden Boot race with five goals in the tournament, Messi described the record-breaking night as 'spectacular' despite feeling 'very tired' after the match.

With six points from two matches, Argentina has now safely advanced to the last 32 of the tournament with a game to spare.

headline_marked: Mushfiqur Rahim [[named ICC Player of the Month]] after Pakistan series
headline: Mushfiqur Rahim named ICC Player of the Month after Pakistan series
summary: The veteran batter becomes only the second Bangladeshi to win the award twice, following a historic home series whitewash against Pakistan.
details: Mushfiqur Rahim has been named the ICC Men’s Player of the Month for May, following his outstanding batting displays during Bangladesh’s historic home series whitewash against Pakistan.
The 39-year-old batter beat teammate Taijul Islam and Nepal’s Dipendra Singh Airee to claim the accolade.
With this win, Mushfiqur becomes only the second Bangladeshi cricketer after Shakib Al Hasan to win the monthly award twice, having previously won it in May 2021.
Mushfiqur played a pivotal role in the 2-0 Test series victory, amassing 253 runs across two matches at an impressive average of 63.25.
His performance included a century and a half-century, which also earned him his first-ever Player of the Series award.
In the opening Test in Mirpur, he hit a vital 71 runs to guide his side to victory.
In the second Test in Sylhet, he scored a commanding 137 runs, marking his 14th Test century.
This century also saw him surpass Mominul Haque to become Bangladesh’s highest century-maker in Test history.
caption:
Mushfiqur Rahim is now the ICC Player of the Month! 

He becomes only the second Bangladeshi to win the award twice.

Mushfiqur Rahim has been named the ICC Men’s Player of the Month for May, following his outstanding batting displays during Bangladesh’s historic home series whitewash against Pakistan.

The 39-year-old batter beat teammate Taijul Islam and Nepal’s Dipendra Singh Airee to claim the accolade.

With this win, Mushfiqur becomes only the second Bangladeshi cricketer after Shakib Al Hasan to win the monthly award twice, having previously won it in May 2021.

Mushfiqur played a pivotal role in the 2-0 Test series victory, amassing 253 runs across two matches at an impressive average of 63.25.

His performance included a century and a half-century, which also earned him his first-ever Player of the Series award.

In the opening Test in Mirpur, he hit a vital 71 runs to guide his side to victory.

In the second Test in Sylhet, he scored a commanding 137 runs, marking his 14th Test century.

This century also saw him surpass Mominul Haque to become Bangladesh’s highest century-maker in Test history.
